practiceQuestions.q: In which year did Muhammad Ghuri first invade India by capturing Multan?
practiceQuestions.sol: Muhammad Ghuri launched his first expedition against India in 1175 CE, capturing Multan and subsequently Uchch. Unlike Mahmud of Ghazni, whose invasions were aimed at plundering wealth, Ghuri's objective was permanent territorial conquest. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following was the ruler of Gujarat when Muhammad Ghuri invaded it in 1178 CE?
practiceQuestions.sol: In 1178 CE, Muhammad Ghuri marched towards Gujarat via the Thar desert. He was decisively defeated by the young Solanki/Chalukya ruler of Gujarat, Mularaja II (with the regency of his mother Nayikadevi), at the Battle of Kayadara. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Medieval Indian History / Standard Historical Canons]

practiceQuestions.q: The First Battle of Tarain was fought in which year?
practiceQuestions.sol: The First Battle of Tarain was fought in 1191 CE between Muhammad Ghuri and the Chahamana (Chauhan) ruler Prithviraj III. Ghuri's army was completely routed, and Ghuri himself was severely wounded by Govinda Rai of Delhi. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who won the Second Battle of Tarain fought in 1192 CE?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Second Battle of Tarain in 1192 CE was won by Muhammad Ghuri. Utilizing superior cavalry tactics and early morning surprise attacks, Ghuri decisively defeated Prithviraj Chauhan, which marked a major turning point in Indian history. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: The Battle of Chandawar (1194 CE) was fought between Muhammad Ghuri and which of the following rulers?
practiceQuestions.sol: In the Battle of Chandawar (1194 CE) near Kanauj, Muhammad Ghuri defeated Jayachandra (Jaichand), the powerful Gahadavala ruler of Kannauj and Banaras, further expanding Turkish control into the Gangetic plains. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which military commander of Muhammad Ghuri was responsible for the conquest of Bengal and Bihar and the destruction of Nalanda University?
practiceQuestions.sol: Ikhtiyar-ud-din Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khilji, a commander under Muhammad Ghuri, led expeditions into Bihar and Bengal, destroying ancient monastic universities like Nalanda and Vikramashila around 1200 CE. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History / ASI Reports]

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following was entrusted with the governance of Muhammad Ghuri's Indian territories after his return to Ghazni, eventually laying the foundation of the Delhi Sultanate?
practiceQuestions.sol: Qutb-ud-din Aibak, a trusted Turkic slave and general of Muhammad Ghuri, was left in charge of Indian conquests. Following Ghuri's assassination in 1206 CE, Aibak established the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty, marking the inception of the Delhi Sultanate. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year was Muhammad Ghuri assassinated?
practiceQuestions.sol: Muhammad Ghuri was assassinated on March 15, 1206 CE, at Dhamiak (now in Pakistan) while on his way back to Ghazni after putting down a revolt in Punjab, reportedly by Khokhars or Ismilis. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which famous Persian chronicler accompanied Muhammad Ghuri on his campaigns and wrote 'Tabaqat-i-Nasiri' later?
practiceQuestions.sol: Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote 'Tabaqat-i-Nasiri', an important historical source detailing the conquests of Muhammad Ghuri and the early years of the Delhi Sultanate. Hasan Nizami wrote 'Taj-ul-Ma'asir' detailing Aibak's campaigns. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Medieval Indian History / Historiographical Standards]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the prime strategic motivation behind Muhammad Ghuri's invasions of Northern India, differentiating him from Mahmud of Ghazni?
opts: Establishment of a permanent Muslim empire in India
Spreading trade relations with Southeast Asia
Forming an alliance against the Seljuk Turks
practiceQuestions.sol: While Mahmud of Ghazni's raids were primarily aimed at extracting wealth and destroying temples to finance his Central Asian empire, Muhammad Ghuri sought to establish political sovereignty and a permanent territorial empire in India. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the military tactics employed by Muhammad Ghuri at the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 CE) differ from and overcome the traditional Indian military setup?
opts: Ghuri relied purely on heavy infantry phalanxes while Indian armies used elephants.
Ghuri utilized highly mobile cavalry archers and feigned retreat tactics, breaking the slow-moving Indian elephant and cavalry formations.
Ghuri used gunpowder artillery which completely terrified the Rajput forces.
Ghuri secured a naval blockade via the Indus river to cut off Rajput supplies.
practiceQuestions.sol: Ghuri divided his cavalry into four units to harass the flanks and rear of the Rajput army, employing feigned retreats to draw them out of formation and then launching coordinated assaults. Rajput reliance on slow war elephants and rigid frontals proved ineffective. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the geopolitical fragmentation of Northern India during the 12th century a primary systemic vulnerability against Ghuri's invasions?
opts: It caused chronic inter-state rivalries, preventing a unified defensive coalition among Rajput states like Chahamanas, Gahadavalas, and Chalukyas.
It led to an acute economic collapse, rendering states bankrupt and unable to maintain armies.
It caused total abandonment of horse breeding and cavalry warfare across all kingdoms.
It forced all monarchs to renounce militarism in favor of pacifist religious doctrines.
practiceQuestions.sol: Northern India was divided among multiple ambitious Rajput dynasties (Chahamanas of Ajmer, Gahadavalas of Kanauj, Chalukyas of Gujarat, Chandellas of Bundelkhand) who were locked in mutual conflicts (e.g., Prithviraj Chauhan's estrangement with Jaichand), making piecemeal defeat inevitable. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Analyze the systemic difference in state-building outcomes between Mahmud of Ghazni's raids and Muhammad Ghuri's invasions.
opts: Ghazni integrated Indian provinces into the Ghaznavid administrative grid, whereas Ghuri maintained temporary tributary relations.
Ghazni operated as a plunder economy extracting wealth to finance Central Asian wars, while Ghuri institutionalized military governorships laying the groundwork for sovereign Islamic rule in India.
Both successfully established continuous dynasties that lasted unbroken through the 13th century.
Ghuri focused solely on maritime trade control in the Arabian Sea, unlike Ghazni's land campaigns.
practiceQuestions.sol: Mahmud of Ghazni viewed India as a perennial source of plunder and revenue extraction without permanent occupation of the Gangetic core. Ghuri realized that long-term control required direct military occupation, assignment of Iqtas, and delegating power to capable Turkic slaves like Aibak. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the establishment of Iqta system during the consolidation phase following Muhammad Ghuri's conquests?
opts: It was a religious taxation system levied exclusively on Hindu pilgrims.
It functioned as a revenue assignment mechanism where military commanders (Iqtadars) collected land revenue to maintain troops and administer conquered tracts.
It was a hereditary feudal estate system granting permanent ownership of land to Indian chiefs.
It served as a central bank regulating currency exchange and gold minting.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Iqta system was a foundational administrative and revenue-assigning institution introduced during the Turkic conquests. Iqtadars were assigned tracts of land from which they collected revenue to maintain military contingents for the Sultanate, ensuring administrative grip without immediate agrarian upheaval. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Muhammad Ghuri manage the succession and political vacuum left after his death in 1206 CE?
opts: He left a clear primogeniture will appointing his biological son as the undisputed Emperor of Ghazni and Delhi.
He left no surviving male heir, prompting his powerful Turkic Mamluk generals (Aibak, Yildiz, Qabacha) to carve out independent domains from his empire.
He abdicated in favor of Prithviraj Chauhan's descendants under a treaty of reconciliation.
He transferred his entire empire to the Caliph of Baghdad directly.
practiceQuestions.sol: Ghuri famously remarked when asked about heirs that he had thousands of sons in his Turkic slaves (Bandagan) who would preserve his empire. Upon his death, his empire fractured among his key slaves: Aibak in Delhi/Lahore, Yildiz in Ghazni, and Qabacha in Sind. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the socio-religious impact of the establishment of Turkic rule following Muhammad Ghuri's campaigns on the Indian subcontinent?
opts: Complete eradication of indigenous faiths and total demographic conversion within a decade.
Introduction of Islamic institutions, Sufi traditions, and urban administrative patterns, initiating a complex process of cultural synthesis and long-term religious pluralism.
Isolation of India from external trade and complete cessation of Indo-Islamic architectural developments.
Abolition of the caste system and immediate establishment of absolute egalitarianism in Hindu society.
practiceQuestions.sol: The establishment of the Delhi Sultanate following Ghuri's conquests did not wipe out existing Indian society; rather, it initiated a vibrant period of interaction between Islamic and Indic traditions, leading to Sufism, new architectural styles (Indo-Islamic), and administrative reforms. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the capture of Delhi and its surrounding doab region critical for the consolidation of Ghuri's empire?
opts: It served as the ultimate gateway controlling communications and logistical routes between the Indus basin and the fertile Gangetic plains.
It was the only source of gold and diamond mines in Northern India.
It housed the naval fleet that guarded against coastal invasions from the south.
It was mandated by the Abbasid Caliph as the capital of all Asian provinces.
practiceQuestions.sol: Delhi's strategic geography as a nexus between the Thar desert, the Himalayas, and the Gangetic doab made it the ideal military and political springboard for dominating Northern India, which explains why subsequent Muslim rulers made it their imperial capital. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the nature of the Turkish military slave system (Bandagan) contribute decisively to the success of Muhammad Ghuri's campaigns?
opts: Slaves were unskilled laborers used solely for building roads and fortifications.
Bandagan were carefully nurtured, highly trained military professionals whose absolute personal loyalty to their master superseded tribal or familial loyalties, ensuring cohesive command.
Slaves were given absolute autonomy to act as independent kings without central oversight.
Slaves served exclusively as religious clerics and legal advisors in judicial courts.
practiceQuestions.sol: The institution of Bandagan provided Ghuri with a cadre of elite military commanders (such as Aibak, Yildiz, Bakhtiyar Khilji) who owed their entire status and loyalty to him. Unburdened by local aristocratic roots, they executed expansionist policies with ruthless efficiency. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the economic consequence of the shift from Ghaznavid raiding to Ghorian conquest in terms of currency and monetary circulation?
opts: Complete demonetization of silver and gold coins across the subcontinent.
Integration of regional currency systems, leading to the introduction of bilingual coins (Arabic and Devanagari) and the stabilization of standard coinage for urban commerce.
Reversal to a barter economy due to the destruction of all trading guilds.
Exclusive use of cowrie shells as legal tender for all high-value transactions.
practiceQuestions.sol: Following the consolidation of Ghorian rule, coinage underwent adaptation. Early Turkish rulers, including Aibak and Ghuri himself, struck coins adopting Indian motifs (like the seated bull and horseman) alongside Arabic inscriptions, facilitating smooth commercial transition before standardizing Islamic coinages like the Tanka. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 / Numismatic Studies]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the geographical location of Ghur (Ghor) shape the strategic orientation of Muhammad Ghuri's empire compared to Ghazni?
opts: Ghur was landlocked and mountainous, forcing Ghuri to seek fertile agricultural outlets and permanent wealth in the Indian plains rather than temporary plunder.
Ghur possessed major ports on the Caspian Sea, giving Ghuri naval supremacy.
Ghur was a flat desert completely dependent on trans-Saharan trade routes.
Ghur's proximity to China enabled direct import of gunpowder weapons.
practiceQuestions.sol: Ghur was situated in the rugged, resource-poor highlands of central Afghanistan. Unlike Ghazni, which sat astride lucrative Central Asian trade routes and reaped vast plunder, Ghur needed sustainable agrarian revenues and territorial control, making Indian conquest an economic necessity. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Invasion of Muhammad Ghuri:
1. Unlike Mahmud of Ghazni, Muhammad Ghuri's primary objective was the establishment of a permanent Muslim empire in India.
2. Muhammad Ghuri suffered a crushing defeat at the hands of the Solanki ruler Mularaja II at the Battle of Kayadara in 1178 CE.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Ghuri sought political control and territorial expansion rather than mere plunder. Statement 2 is also correct: in 1178 CE, Ghuri invaded Gujarat and was severely defeated by Mularaja II and his mother Nayikadevi at Kayadara near Mount Abu. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 & 11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battles of Tarain:
1. In the First Battle of Tarain (1191 CE), Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghuri, but failed to follow up his victory by capturing Ghazni or expelling Turkish garrisons from Bhatinda.
2. In the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 CE), Prithviraj Chauhan was aided by Jaichand of Kanauj, leading to a massive Rajput coalition against Ghuri.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Prithviraj captured Bhatinda fort after a long siege following Tarain I, but failed to pursue Ghuri back to Central Asia or secure the frontier permanently. Statement 2 is incorrect: Jaichand of Kanauj was hostile to Prithviraj (due to the abduction of Samyukta and political rivalry) and did not aid him; in fact, Jaichand was defeated separately by Ghuri in 1194 CE at Chandawar. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Chandawar (1194 CE):
1. It was fought between Muhammad Ghuri and Jayachandra of the Gahadavala dynasty.
2. The victory at Chandawar opened the gates of the fertile Gangetic doab and Banaras for Turkish expansion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Battle of Chandawar resulted in the defeat and death of Jayachandra, breaking the formidable Gahadavala military power and enabling Ghuri's forces to occupy Kanauj, Banaras, and advance into eastern India. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Ikhtiyar-ud-din Bakhtiyar Khilji:
1. He was a prominent military general of Muhammad Ghuri who conquered Bihar and Bengal.
2. He was responsible for the destruction of the ancient Buddhist monastic university of Nalanda.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Bakhtiyar Khilji led Turkic incursions into eastern India, unseated Lakshmanasena of the Sena dynasty in Bengal, and sacked major monastic centers like Nalanda and Vikramashila as documented in Persian chronicles like Tabaqat-i-Nasiri. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History / ASI]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administration and legacy of Muhammad Ghuri:
1. Muhammad Ghuri issued gold coins bearing the image of Goddess Lakshmi on one side and Arabic inscriptions on the other.
2. After Ghuri's death in 1206 CE, his Indian possessions were unified under a single centralized empire ruled directly by his biological son Aram Shah.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Ghuri issued coins featuring the image of Goddess Lakshmi to facilitate commercial acceptance among his newly conquered non-Muslim subjects. Statement 2 is incorrect: Ghuri had no surviving son; Aram Shah (whose relation to Aibak/Ghuri is disputed) was a weak ruler briefly installed in Lahore/Delhi, and the empire fragmented among Ghuri's slave generals Aibak, Yildiz, and Qabacha. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / Numismatic Records]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the sources of history for Muhammad Ghuri's campaigns:
1. 'Tabaqat-i-Nasiri' was authored by Minhaj-us-Siraj and provides valuable information on Ghuri's conquests.
2. 'Taj-ul-Ma'asir', written by Hasan Nizami, is a primary Persian chronicle detailing the military campaigns of Qutb-ud-din Aibak under Ghuri.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Minhaj-us-Siraj's Tabaqat-i-Nasiri and Hasan Nizami's Taj-ul-Ma'asir are foundational contemporary Persian literary sources that document the transition of power from the Ghurids to the Delhi Sultanate. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Medieval Indian History / Historiographical Survey]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the causes of Rajput defeat against Muhammad Ghuri:
1. Lack of political unity and mutual antagonism among Northern Indian Rajput principalities prevented a combined defense.
2. Continued reliance on slow-moving war elephants and rigid frontal infantry formations proved disastrous against Ghuri's mobile cavalry archers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are accurate representations of standard historical consensus. Political fragmentation and tactical obsolescence (over-reliance on war elephants and lack of mobile cavalry tactics) were primary structural reasons for the defeat of Indian armies. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, Medieval India / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the assassination of Muhammad Ghuri:
1. He was assassinated in 1206 CE by a group of disgruntled Khokhars or Ismilis while camping at Dhamiak in Punjab.
2. His death instantly resulted in the peaceful coronation of his nephew as the sole Emperor of Delhi and Ghazni without any military conflict.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Ghuri was killed in March 1206 CE at Dhamiak by rebels (frequently identified as Khokhars). Statement 2 is incorrect: His death led to a fierce struggle for succession among his top Mamluk generals (Aibak, Yildiz, Qabacha) and other regional claimants, fracturing the empire rather than producing a peaceful unified coronation. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the geopolitical impact of the Ghurids in South Asia:
1. The Ghurid conquests permanently severed India's overland trade routes with Central Asia and West Asia.
2. The establishment of Turkic rule integrated Northern India into a broader Afro-Eurasian trade and Islamic administrative network.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Ghurid conquests actually reconnected Northern India directly with Central Asian and West Asian trade and cultural circuits, intensifying overland exchange. Statement 2 is correct: Turkic governance integrated the subcontinent into the wider Islamic world system, boosting urbanism, monetization, and diplomatic exchanges. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / Economic History of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the military strategy of Muhammad Ghuri:
1. Unlike Mahmud of Ghazni who launched lightning annual raids and retreated, Ghuri established permanent military outposts and governors to secure conquered territories.
2. Ghuri's military victories in Northern India relied entirely on naval supremacy in the Arabian Sea and Indian Ocean.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Ghuri differed from Ghazni by instituting permanent territorial administration through military governors (Iqtadars) and trusted slave commanders. Statement 2 is blatantly incorrect: Ghuri's campaigns were entirely land-based operations conducted across the Indus basin and Gangetic plains; he possessed no naval forces in the Arabian Sea. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Medieval Indian History]
